sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a small, friendly Archaeopteryx, an early feathered bird-dinosaur with soft teal and blue feathers, standing on two little feet, turned to the left. Draw this exact Archaeopteryx as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, feather texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body with its neck: the plump body with its soft cream chest and teal feathered back and sides, turned as in image 1, without head, without wings, without legs and without tail: no wings, feet or tail feathers drawn on it. At the top, the cream throat and the teal feathered back of the neck go straight up, as wide as the neck is under the head in image 1, and end in a soft, smooth edge with NO outline (it is hidden under the head). At the back, the teal back ends in a soft edge cut straight down, with NO outline across it (the tail tucks under it): no stump, no round bump, no line where the tail would join. The drawing's dark outline runs only along the front of the chest, round the tummy and along the back.
2. the head alone, without neck: the round teal head with its crest of soft blue feathers sweeping back, the cream throat patch under where the beak would be and the rosy cheek, turned to the left as in image 1, with a completely blank face: no eyes, no eyebrows, no beak, no mouth line; where the beak would be, the front of the face is rounded off smoothly. Keep its dark outline over the top of the head and the crest, and round the front of the face; from the chin round to the back of the head its bottom edge is soft, with NO outline: the feathers simply stop there.
3. the near folded wing (the big wing lying over the body on the right in image 1): teal and blue layered feathers with paler tips, folded against the side as in image 1, with three little round clawless fingers peeking at the bend of its front edge, drawn whole, its top shoulder end a full rounded edge with its outline as in image 1.
4. the far folded wing (the bit of teal wing peeking out behind the chest on the left in image 1): the same wing of the other side, folded down, drawn whole including what is normally hidden behind the chest, its top shoulder end a smooth rounded edge with no outline across it.
5. the near wing open: the same near wing spread out wide and raised as in flight, reaching out up and to the right, its long teal and blue flight feathers fanned out with paler tips, three little round clawless fingers at the bend of its front edge, a smooth rounded shoulder end at its root on the lower left, with no outline across it.
6. the far wing open: the same wing of the other side spread out wide and raised as in flight, reaching out up and to the left, seen a little shorter as it is farther away, three little round clawless fingers at the bend of its front edge, a smooth rounded shoulder end at its root on the lower right, with no outline across it.
7. the far leg: the leg on the left of image 1, its fluffy teal feathered thigh and its orange scaly shin and little foot with three soft, round, blunt toes, drawn whole from the top of the thigh (normally hidden under the body), its top a smooth rounded end with no outline across it.
8. the near leg: the leg on the right of image 1, its fluffy teal feathered thigh and its orange scaly shin and little foot with three soft, round, blunt toes, drawn whole from the top of the thigh, its top a smooth rounded end with no outline across it.
9. the long feathery tail: teal and blue feathers fanned along it with paler tips, curving up at its end as in image 1, drawn whole from its thin base (normally hidden behind the body) to the tip; its base a smooth rounded end with no outline across it.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. Nothing sharp: no teeth, no claws. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a small, friendly Archaeopteryx, a feathered bird-dinosaur; image 2 shows the same Archaeopteryx cut into puppet parts, with a blank face and no beak. Draw the Archaeopteryx's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the Archaeopteryx in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2. Its head is turned to the left: its far eye (on the left of image 1, just above the beak) is smaller and narrower than its near eye (on the right of image 1). In image 1 both eyes look up and to the left: each big dark-brown iris sits towards the upper left of its eye, the white on its right.

Draw each piece on its own, upright, in four tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
Row 1, the far eye (the smaller, narrower eye, on the LEFT of image 1), six times:
1. as it is in image 1: a big dark-brown iris with a white sparkle, looking up and to the left.
2. wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, with its white sparkle, looking the same way.
3. closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc, like an upside-down U, with a few small lashes.
4. sad: open, the dark-brown iris with a white sparkle looking down and to the left, a thin shine along its bottom rim; no lid slanting across it.
5. crying: squeezed shut, a soft lid line as wide as the open eye, curving down at both ends like a little frown (a sad closed eye, not a smile), and one small light-blue teardrop just below it.
6. gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line as wide as the open eye, with a few short lashes.
Row 2, the near eye (the bigger eye, on the RIGHT of image 1), the same six in the same order; open, it looks the same way as row 1, up and to the left, the iris towards the upper left of the eye.
Row 3: 13. the far eyebrow (over the left eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 14. the same far eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (right) end. 15. the near eyebrow (over the right eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a thin dark-brown arch. 16. the same near eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (left) end.
Row 4, the short orange beak, pointing to the left as in image 1, its base on the right a smooth rounded edge with no line across it (it tucks onto the face), none with any teeth:
17. the beak closed in a smile, as in image 1, its mouth line curling up at the corner.
18. the same beak open wide in a happy laugh: the upper beak lifted, the lower beak dropped, the inside smooth and pink with a little pink tongue.
19. the same beak closed, sad: its mouth line turning down at the corner.
20. the same beak a little open in surprise: a small round opening, smooth and pink inside.
21. the same beak open in a happy chirpy song: open halfway, pointing a little upward, smooth and pink inside with a little tongue.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the archaeopteryx flies along to the left on quick, flappy little wingbeats, a bit wobbly, then flutters down, lands with a little stumble and folds its wings.
the archaeopteryx hops along to the left on both little feet, hop after hop, wings folded, then stops.
the archaeopteryx spreads its wings and flaps them quickly, a little clumsily, its feet staying on the ground.

pause.shows: the archaeopteryx with its wings spread wide

animations.description: the archaeopteryx crouches, jumps up high for joy with its wings out and lands with a little squash.
the archaeopteryx shakes its head no.
the archaeopteryx looks up, then turns right round to look behind it, then turns back and looks ahead again.

pause.shows: the archaeopteryx turned round, looking behind it

animations.description: the archaeopteryx does a happy little dance, swaying from side to side, its wings out a little and its tail swishing.
the archaeopteryx cries, head down, its little shoulders shaking with sobs.

pause.shows: the archaeopteryx crying, head down, eyes squeezed shut with tears

animations.description: the archaeopteryx gives a big yawn, fluffs up, tucks its head down and falls asleep, then wakes up, blinks and smiles.

pause.shows: the archaeopteryx fast asleep, fluffed up, eyes shut, head drooped

animations.description: the archaeopteryx lifts its wing and waves hello.
the archaeopteryx shivers and trembles, cold or scared, its wings pulled in tight.
the archaeopteryx puffs up its chest, tips its head back and sings a happy chirpy song, then flicks its tail and smiles.

pause.shows: the archaeopteryx singing, head tipped back, beak open, eyes closed

animations.description: the archaeopteryx tucks its beak into the soft feathers of its chest and wing and tidies them, nibble-nibble, then shakes and smooths itself down.

pause.shows: the archaeopteryx with its beak tucked into its feathers, tidying them

animations.description: the archaeopteryx bends down and pecks at the ground, peck-peck-peck, then looks up happily.

pause.shows: the archaeopteryx bent forward, its beak down to the ground

animations.description: the archaeopteryx fluffs out all its feathers until it is round and cosy, settles with a happy sigh, then smooths them down again.

pause.shows: the archaeopteryx fluffed up round and cosy, eyes closed

animations.description: the archaeopteryx stretches one wing out wide and its leg out behind it, holds the stretch, then tucks them back in.

pause.shows: the archaeopteryx stretching one wing out wide and its leg out behind
